idiom_name: http.Handler middleware chain over a policy-decision function/enforcer
implementation_notes: Go has no authorization abstraction in net/http, but the middleware chain is the language's own enforcement point: a func(http.Handler) http.Handler wraps the mux, obtains a decision for the request and returns before next.ServeHTTP on denial, so handlers never check rules themselves. The decision is an ordinary function or a policy library - Casbin keeps the model in a PERM configuration and answers with Enforcer.Enforce(sub, obj, act) - which gives the decision/store split without a class hierarchy. Chain the guard per route group (RequirePermission(...) around /admin/) so new endpoints are registered inside the guarded subtree rather than beside it.
pitfalls: A handler registered on the root mux instead of inside the guarded sub-mux bypasses the middleware silently; guard at the outermost mux with a catch-all deny.
Reloading policies concurrently against a plain *casbin.Enforcer races; use the synced enforcer or swap the enforcer behind an atomic pointer.
Goroutines started by a handler outlive the request: the decision is per request, so the principal must be passed explicitly instead of stored on the handler.
